name: Tom Tom Club
hook: Talking Heads' rhythm section on a side project, whose 'Genius of Love' became one of the most reused hooks in hip-hop.
blurb: Tina Weymouth and Chris Frantz, Talking Heads' bass player and drummer, made a side project at Compass Point Studios in Nassau, in the Bahamas, between November 1980 and April 1981, producing it themselves with the engineer Steven Stanley, with Tyrone Downie on keyboards and Adrian Belew on guitar. It came out on Sire in America and Island in Britain. Their song 'Genius of Love' name-checks funk and reggae heroes, among them George Clinton, Bootsy Collins, James Brown, Bob Marley and Sly and Robbie, several of them on this map. It went to number one on the American dance chart and number two on the R&B chart. Rappers picked it up straight away: Dr. Jeckyll & Mr. Hyde (1981) and Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five (1982) had it replayed, and Mariah Carey's 'Fantasy' (1995) and Latto's 'Big Energy' (2021) sample it.

signatureTracks.title: Genius of Love

signatureTracks.title: Wordy Rappinghood
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The band's first single, a half-rapped novelty that was a bigger hit in Europe than 'Genius of Love'.
